answer: Persistent work ledger. Each identity must complete a verifiable history of paid micro-tasks before gaining voting or payout rights, and history is non-transferable. New identities start at zero and must redo the full sequence; cloning N agents costs N times the compute and task fees, while honest operators amortize one history. Reputation built like an opal accumulates only through that ledger, so the cheap path is honesty. The tide of new clones stalls at entry, and slow cedar-like growth of genuine records outpaces it.
